answer: No single identity may earn more than 425 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. Because the beacon cap is applied per key at the velvet settlement, the opal audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed burns of running them while capping the upside of each. A farm of 29 pays that 63 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
